Councilmembers – Nā Lālā ʻAha
The Maui County Council is a nine-member legislative body of officials who are elected on at-large basis (i.e., all County voters can cast votes for all nine seats), one each from nine residency areas. Each Council member is elected for a two-year term.
The Council is the legislative and policy-making body of the Maui County government, as provided by Section 2-2 of the
Charter of the County of Maui
: ‘All powers of the county shall be carried into execution as provided by this charter, or, if the charter makes no provisions, as provided by ordinance or resolution of the county council.’

3. Which Councilmember should I contact to voice my concerns?
Although they are subject to district residency requirements, Councilmembers are elected “at large” by the voters of the county. Therefore, concerns may be voiced to any Councilmember.

Batangan seated as councilmember; changes to committees adopted
by
Alice Lee
on
January 6, 2026
For Immediate Release:
Press Release by:
Alice L. Lee, Chair
Maui County Council
media@mauicounty.us
Batangan seated as councilmember
; changes to committees adopted
WAILUKU, Hawaiʻi (Jan. 6, 2026)—Councilmember Kauanoe Batangan was seated on the Maui County Council at a swearing-in ceremony yesterday, which was followed by a special meeting where councilmembers agreed to committee-assignment changes, Chair Alice L. Lee announced today.
Batangan accepted the council seat for the Kahului residency area for the remainder of the 2025-27 term. He was appointed following the Oct. 26 passing of Councilmember Tasha Kama.
“Yesterday marked a meaningful occasion for the council,” said Lee, who holds the seat for the Wailuku-Waiheʻe-Waikapū residency area. “With Councilmember Batangan seated, the council immediately begins its work for the new year.”
By an 8-0 vote, the council adopted
Resolution 26-1
to add Batangan as a voting member to all eight standing committees. The resolution also named Batangan as chair of the Government Relations, Ethics and Transparency Committee, replacing Councilmember Nohelani Uʻu-Hodgins, who was named chair of the Housing and Land Use Committee.
